newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Wednesday's Commission briefing.

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Wednesday:

Spokesman Willy Helin briefed on the Commission decision to propose the Industry Council adopt, on April 24, measures for shipyard restructuring in Spain, Germany and Greece Helin said the Commission regretted that the United States continued to provide aid to its shipyards and that it was not always done in a transparent way.
In answer to a question, Helin said German metals and engineering group Hoesch-Krupp had not formally notified the Commission of its plans to take over Thyssen AG.

Asked to react to the WTO trade disputes panel interim report that EU banana import quotas violated open trading rules, spokesman Peter Guilford said that the Commission would need to analyse the report in order to make sure that none of the conclusions were based on a misunderstanding of the facts. He said that if there was such a misunderstanding, the Commission would possibly ask for an interim review. Guilford also said that if the Commission thought the legal reasoning of the interim report was faulty, it would retain its right to request appeal.
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said the decision taken 18 months ago to suspend all contacts and to deny visas to senior members of the Nigerian junta was still in force.
Spokeswoman Barbara Nolan said the delays in budget support for the disabled were on their way to being resolved.

Vale de Almeida said spokeswoman Lousewies van der Laan would hold a briefing in her office at 1515/1415 GMT on the new guidelines for the PHARE programme in the framework of pre-membership if the Commission had taken a decision by then on this issue.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/97/230: Commission questions Denmark's total ban on metal cans for drinks.
- IP/97/231: Commission takes further legal action against Portugal and Ireland for failing to respect EU rules on the protection of waters against nitrate pollution.
- IP/97/232: Commission takes further legal action against the United Kingdom for failing to respect EU rules on the protection of groundwater.
- IP/97/233: Sexual harassment in the workplace: second stage consultation of the social partners.
- IP/97/235: Commission proposes Industry Ministers to clear restructuring aid for Spanish, German and Greek shipyards.
- IP/97/236: Commission begins an in-depth investigation of the Boeing/McDonell Douglas Merger.
